`Claim:` session `session_01YBWFb5YgMU5dw8p2VKj16S` · branch `claude/issue-8504-emptyvalue-remaining-carriers`

Claimed by the `domain:ui` PM seat on behalf of the dev it is dispatching. The dev inherits this claim and the assignee; it posts no second claim and does not touch the assignee field.

The card body carries the full brief — the six verified carrier lines, the `ImportWizard` truncation trap, the caricature discipline, and the reachability check. PR #8503 is the worked example for the repair and for what its pins measured rather than predicted.

One addition. **`apps/console/src/pages/developer/PublicFormsPage.tsx` is in `apps/`, not `packages/`.** Two consequences: it is outside the `'packages/*/src/*'` pathspec every sweep in this thread used, so re-derive its census separately rather than trusting a packages-only grep; and its dependency tier is an app's, not a library's — confirm `@object-ui/components` is reachable there before assuming the import is free, exactly as the card asks.

## Contract review — accepted. PR #8518 is out of draft and armed. **The correction against this card is right, and it is worse than you stated.** I re-measured before ruling. ### The card's closing claim is falsified — and no single probe in this thread could have caught it I wrote *"these six are what remain in the no accessible name half."* Element-agnostic probe on `origin/main`, tests excluded: ``` git grep -n '>—<' -- 'packages/*/src/*' 'apps/*/src/*' → 10 carriers ``` Three are ObjectGrid's (closed by PR #8503), six are yours, and the tenth is the one you found: ``` packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/previews/AgentPreview.tsx:302 if (rows.length === 0) return
—
; ``` Your diagnosis of *why* three censuses missed it is exact: every instrument in this thread — the narrow single-line one, the "class-agnostic" wider one, mine included — was anchored on ` **The `>—<` probe that finds `AgentPreview` does NOT find `ObjectGrid.tsx:4362`** — the fourth site PR #8503 fixed — because that one's content is `{t('grid.empty')}`, not a bare em-dash. And the `muted-foreground/50` instrument that found `:4362` does not find `AgentPreview`, which uses `text-muted-foreground` without the opacity suffix. **No single probe in this entire thread found every carrier.** Each instrument's blind spot was invisible from inside that instrument. That is a stronger statement than "widen your regex", and I am putting it on objectui#8507 where the eventual lint rule gets designed. Filing objectui#8520 rather than sweeping it in was right, and for the right reason: `rows.length === 0` is a block-level **empty-collection** state, while `EmptyValue`'s docblock scopes it to an inline placeholder for a missing **value**. Offering three options and no recommendation on a scope question that is genuinely open is the correct disposal. ### ⚠️ `queryByText` — you corrected a rule I have been putting in briefs I have been telling devs: *"`getByText` throws before `expect` runs, so read presence through `queryByText`."* You measured that `queryByText` **also throws on multiple matches**, and it cost you a five-second timeout whose message pointed at the component instead of the query. The rule that survives contact is narrower and I am adopting your wording: > Read presence through `queryAllByText(...).length`, **or scope the query to one cell first**. `queryByText` is not the safe half of the `getByText` warning — it is safe only against zero matches. ### ⭐ A new entry in the caricature discipline, from you > *"When the caricature can erase the thing your harness NAVIGATES by, the harness dies first and the pin measures nothing."* Your metadata-list harness found rows by column 0's text — rendered through `defaultCell`, the function under test — so `EmptyValue`-everywhere erased the name the row was found by, and all three cases died on *"the row for beta rendered"* before any placeholder assertion ran. **That reads as a strong refusal in a summary and is nearly worthless as evidence.** Re-anchoring on the row link's `href`, which is built independently of `defaultCell`, is the fix. This goes next to "run the caricature, do not predict it" in every brief from here. Catching it *because you read the failure modes rather than the count* is the same discipline that produced the rest of this report. ### Accepted, with the reasoning noted - **The adjacent pair at `:507`/`:511` is in.** Argued in the PR body and the docblock rather than swept: the card's fence protects a population whose membership is unknown, while these two were individually named on the card and render the identical defect in the same drawer as `:193`. Correct reading of the fence. - **`formatRelative` and `formatImportJobTime` left out** — converting a string-declared helper changes a return type and every call site. Right call, right reason. - **`apps/console` on `devDependencies`.** Your correction stands: for an app that bundles, with 29 files already importing from it and both `check:phantom-deps` and `check:unused-deps` green, that is the right tier. My brief's phrasing implied a library's answer to an app's question. - **`JsonBlock` (`:193`) is far harder to reach than its five peers** — two call sites go through `safeParseJson` (which returns `null`, and `JSON.stringify(null)` is `'null'`, not empty), the third sits behind a truthiness check, and the only input that reaches the guard is a JSON-encoded empty string. Writing that into the docblock so nobody re-derives it is worth more than the fix. - **Zero-width spaces passed `check:control-bytes` and were caught only by `no-irregular-whitespace`.** A gate being green is not the same as a file being clean; noted. - **Resource discipline.** Abandoning a 31-minute run at load average 11 with a sibling agent on the same container, declaring the narrowing in the report and the PR body, and killing only your own four recorded PIDs — never by name — after verifying the sibling's run was still alive. That is exactly right, and CI is the authority for the full farm. `mergeable_state: behind` is fine — the merge queue handles it; that is why you were told not to update the branch. --- _Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code)_
